question: Which configuration statically assigns VSAN membership to a virtual Fibre Channel interface?
theory: VSAN membership for a virtual Fibre Channel interface can be assigned statically from the VSAN database using 'vsan <id> interface vfc <n>', which directly binds that interface to the VSAN regardless of what traffic or FCoE mapping is configured elsewhere. This is distinct from binding a vfc to its underlying Ethernet interface (done under the vfc interface itself with the 'bind interface' command) - the VSAN database command specifically controls VSAN port membership, not the FCoE binding. (CCNP/CCIE DCCOR Official Cert Guide, Chapter 8 - VSAN)
